user.title: Weishaupt
user.description: How does this Home Assistant reach the heating system? Through the bridge Weishaupt2MQTT (an add-on that holds ebusd, the Weishaupt definitions and the write guards, and publishes on MQTT), or through an ebusd you run yourself.

bridge.title: Weishaupt2MQTT (MQTT)
bridge.description: Base topic of the bridge Weishaupt2MQTT. The bridge must be running and Home Assistant's MQTT integration must be set up on the same broker: the bridge is looked for on this topic before the entry is created. Nothing is published, and nothing is written to the heating system unless writes are enabled later in the options.

data_description.base_topic: Base topic configured in Weishaupt2MQTT (default: weishaupt).

manual.title: ebusd
manual.description: Address of the ebusd that is connected to the heating system. ebusd must have loaded a release of the Weishaupt definitions. Nothing is written to the heating system unless writes are enabled later in the options.

data_description.host: Host name or IP address of ebusd.
data_description.port: TCP command port of ebusd, 8888 unless it was changed.

reconfigure.title: Weishaupt
reconfigure.description: Change what the Configure button (which opens the panel) does not: MQTT bridge (Weishaupt2MQTT), the ebusd this entry uses, the load it puts on the bus and its writes, and the telegram log of each ebusd.

menu_options.endpoints: ebusd (the list, and which one to use)

mqtt.title: Weishaupt2MQTT (MQTT)
mqtt.description: Connect to the heating system through Weishaupt2MQTT using Home Assistant's MQTT integration. Existing devices, entities, history and options are kept.

data_description.base_topic: Base topic configured in Weishaupt2MQTT (default: weishaupt).

endpoints.title: ebusd
endpoints.description: New address of the ebusd in use. The entry, its devices, entities, history and options are kept.

data_description.host: Host name or IP address of ebusd.
data_description.port: TCP command port of ebusd, 8888 unless it was changed.

addons.title: ebusd
addons.description: The ebusd add-ons found on this Home Assistant. Tick each one this integration may use: they run one at a time (one adapter), and the integration uses the one that is running. A stopped add-on is kept without being tested. You can also enter the address of an ebusd elsewhere. Nothing is written to the heating system unless writes are enabled later in the options.

data_description.addons: Name, host name and state of each ebusd add-on.
data_description.host: Optional: host name or IP address of an ebusd that is not an add-on of this Home Assistant.
data_description.port: TCP command port of that ebusd, 8888 unless it was changed.

reconfigure_addons.title: ebusd
reconfigure_addons.description: The ebusd add-ons and the other ebusd this integration may use. The entry, its devices, entities, history and options are kept.

data_description.addons: Name, host name and state of each ebusd add-on.
data_description.host: Optional: host name or IP address of an ebusd that is not an add-on of this Home Assistant. Empty: none.
data_description.port: TCP command port of that ebusd, 8888 unless it was changed.

reconfigure_use.title: Which ebusd
reconfigure_use.description: Follow the running ebusd: the integration uses the one that answers with a signal on the bus, and moves to another known one when the one in use stops answering. Pinned: it uses that one only. The entry reloads: entities and history are kept, the write switch is off, the build is checked again.

settings.title: Bus load and writes

data.writes_enabled: Enable writes of the proven settings
data.allow_stock_writes: Allow writes on a stock ebusd (non-boiler controllers)

data_description.request_gap: The integration never sends two requests closer together than this.
data_description.cyclic_interval: How often temperatures and other live values are read. Settings, counters and programs are read far less often.
data_description.writes_enabled: Creates a number entity for each setting a release of the definitions proves writable, and the write switch (off). By default a write needs an ebusd build that computes the run-time checksum (john30/ebusd#1825), checked without sending anything to the bus; the option below lifts that for the non-boiler controllers. Regulation settings are written only after a confirmation in Settings > Repairs.
data_description.allow_stock_writes: Allow writes to the non-boiler controllers (system manager, heating modules, room units) on a stock ebusd that does not compute the run-time checksum. On-site validation on 2026-11-23 showed a stock ebusd 26.1 writes every published setting of these controllers end to end; the write then carries the checksum byte of the definition, which the controllers accept. The boiler automats are never written on a stock ebusd, and the build is still required for them. Leave off if you run the build with the run-time checksum (john30/ebusd#1825).
data_description.max_writes_per_hour: Writes accepted within any sliding hour (1 to 200, default 30). The limit protects the memory of the regulators from wear: keep 30 in normal service. A higher value is only for a supervised test campaign; set it back to 30 when the campaign ends. Changing it reloads the integration, which restarts the count.

settings.description: Load on the bus, and writes. Writes are off unless enabled here; then a write switch on the ebusd device turns them on and off, and only the settings the definitions prove writable can be set. Changing this reloads the integration.

telegram_log.title: Telegram log
telegram_log.description: Each ebusd add-on keeps its own telegram log (its option sqlite_db). Choose the ebusd whose log path you want to set.

telegram_log_path.title: Telegram log of {label}
telegram_log_path.description: Path of the SQLite telegram log this ebusd keeps. A write from the address of the vendor service tool (ff) is refused while the tool may be connected, and when this log cannot be read or is not fed. Changing this reloads the integration.

error.cannot_connect: No ebusd answers at this address.
error.mqtt_not_available: Home Assistant's MQTT integration is not set up. Add it (Settings > Devices & services > Add integration > MQTT) on the broker the bridge publishes to, then try again.
error.no_bridge: No Weishaupt2MQTT bridge was found on this base topic: bridge/state did not read online, or bridge/info did not arrive within 5 seconds. Check that the bridge is started, its base topic, and that it uses the same broker as Home Assistant.
error.bridge_offline: The Weishaupt2MQTT bridge on this base topic is offline (bridge/state reads offline). Start it, then try again.
error.invalid_topic: Not a base topic: no +, no # and no empty level.

abort.bridge_already_configured: The bridge on this base topic is already configured.

ebusd.title: Which ebusd
ebusd.description: In use now: {label}. Follow the running ebusd: the integration uses the one that answers with a signal on the bus, and moves to another known one when the one in use stops answering. Pinned: it uses that one only. Changing this reloads the integration: entities and history are kept, the write switch is off, the build is checked again. No add-on is started or stopped.

definitions_mismatch.title: The definitions loaded by ebusd are not those this integration expects
definitions_mismatch.description:
{count} messages of the Weishaupt definitions {version} are missing in ebusd ({missing}) or defined differently ({different}): {messages}.

These values are not shown. Load a release of the definitions in the range {accepted} in ebusd (with `--scanconfig`), then reload the integration.

no_devices.title: No Weishaupt device found on the bus
no_devices.description:
ebusd answers, but none of the addresses the Weishaupt definitions describe is on its bus. Other addresses seen: {addresses}.

Check that ebusd has a signal and has scanned the bus, then reload the integration.

confirm.title: {setting} — {device}

abort.expired: This request has expired or was withdrawn: nothing was written. Set the value again to create a new one.
abort.not_taken: {setting} of {device}: {requested} was sent and acknowledged, but the controller reads back {read_back}. The value was not taken over.
abort.write_failed: {setting} of {device}: the write was not sent ({reason}).
abort.no_read_back: {setting} of {device}: {requested} was sent, but could not be read back ({reason}). Check the value before trying again.

create_entry.written: Done. {setting} of {device}: {requested} written and read back from the controller ({read_back}). Telegram `{telegram}`.
create_entry.unchanged: {setting} of {device} already holds {requested}: nothing was written.

confirm_clock.title: Confirm: set the clock of the installation

confirm.title: Set the clock — {device}
confirm.description:
- Clock master now: {current} against the clock of ebusd's host
- Will send **{send_at}** at {send_at} exactly ({requested}, at second 00 of the next minute). If you confirm after that minute has begun, the next minute is used
- Broadcast to bus address `{address}`, command `{register}`, from source address `{source}` ({source_text})

Every controller takes the time over, seconds included. If the bus is not free within {late} s of second 00, nothing is sent.

abort.expired: This request has expired or was withdrawn: nothing was written. Set the value again to create a new one.
abort.write_failed: {setting} of {device}: the write was not sent ({reason}).
abort.clock_late: The connection to ebusd was not free within {late} s of second 00: the time was not sent, rather than sent late.

create_entry.sent: Done. The time {sent} was broadcast at second 00 ({late_ms} ms after it). Telegram `{telegram}`. The offset sensor shows the result after the next broadcast of the clock master.

stale_entities.title: Entities no longer in the definitions
stale_entities.description:
The definitions in use ({version}) no longer have these entities: {entities}.

They were kept because you changed them (name, icon, area, labels, aliases, hidden or disabled, display options). They will not get values again. Remove them in Settings → Devices & services → Entities when you no longer need them; this repair then goes away at the next reload.

definitions_file.title: Definitions file beside the configuration: not used
definitions_file.description:
Definitions in use: {version} ({source}).

Files of the folder `weishaupt` of the configuration that were not used, and why: {refused}.

A definitions file is used only when its sha256 matches the `sha256sums` file of the same release beside it, its schema is the one this version reads, and its version is newer than the bundled one and within the accepted range. Fix or remove the file, then reload the integration.

old_entities.title: Entities left by version 0.1 of the integration ({count})

confirm.title: Remove the entities left by version 0.1

abort.no_entry: The integration entry is not loaded: nothing was removed.
abort.nothing_left: No entity of version 0.1 is left: nothing to remove.

create_entry.removed: {count} entities of version 0.1 were removed from the registry.

device_absent.title: {device} has not been on the bus for {days} days

confirm.title: Remove {device}
confirm.description:
{device} has not answered on the bus for days. If it was removed from the installation, remove it from Home Assistant: the device and its entities are deleted from the registries, their history stays in the recorder until it is purged.

If it is only switched off, leave it: it comes back by itself when it answers again, and this repair goes away.

Nothing is removed until you confirm here.

abort.no_entry: The integration entry is not loaded: nothing was removed.
abort.device_back: The device answers again or was already removed: nothing to do.

ebusd_not_running.title: ebusd {label} does not answer
ebusd_not_running.description:
The ebusd this integration uses does not answer, and no other known ebusd answers either. Its entities are unavailable until one does. Start the ebusd add-on you use (Settings > Add-ons), or check the address under Devices & services > Weishaupt > Reconfigure.

{endpoints}

choose.title: Use another ebusd
choose.description: {label} does not answer, and another known ebusd does. Choose it, or let the integration follow the running ebusd. The integration reloads; no add-on is started or stopped and nothing is sent to the bus.

abort.no_entry: The integration entry is not there any more: nothing was changed.
abort.none_answers: No other ebusd answers now: nothing was changed.

create_entry.switched: The integration now uses the ebusd you chose.

ebusd_several.title: Several ebusd answer with a signal
ebusd_several.description: {labels} answer with a signal on the bus. One adapter should serve one ebusd at a time. The integration keeps {label} and does not switch between them. Stop the ebusd add-on you do not use, or pin one in the options (Which ebusd).

program_shared.message: This program is read from the store of {device}: a change sent to this device would be acknowledged and lost. Change {program} of {device}.

switch_off.message: The write switch is off: turn it on to write (it is off after every restart of Home Assistant or reload of the integration).

writes_disabled.message: Writes are not enabled in the options of the integration: enable them there, then turn the write switch on.

capability_absent.message: This ebusd does not compute the run-time checksum (john30/ebusd#1825). Enable "Allow writes on a stock ebusd" in the options to write the non-boiler controllers through it; the boiler automats are never written on a stock ebusd.

capability_unknown.message: Whether ebusd computes the run-time checksum is not known ({reason}): writes refused.

source_not_own.message: {setting} is proven written from address 31 only, and the address of this ebusd is {own}.

set_program.name: Set a weekly program
set_program.description: Writes days of a weekly program of a room unit at once: only the slots that change, three at most a day (21 for a whole week), within the hourly write limit. When more slots would change than writes are left within the hour, nothing is written.
